correctness.rationale: The interaction, dephasing jump, faithful initial state, and scaling satisfy the source hypotheses. The mean-field interaction vanishes because \(\operatorname{tr}(m_tZ)=0\). The local dephasing and Ising Hamiltonian generators commute, giving the exact factorized state. Direct conjugation yields the cosine-power one-site expectation. Unitary invariance of entropy plus \(\log m_t=\alpha_tI+\operatorname{artanh}(r_t)X\) gives the finite-\(N\) Umegaki identity, and the Taylor expansion of \(\log\cos(2Jt/N)\) gives the positive \(N\mathfrak H_N\) limit. A standalone enumerator independently rechecks finite phase sums. The proof, not the finite checks, covers all \(N\).

value.rationale: The finding resolves a natural question left by a new quantitative theorem: whether its \(N^{-1}\) entropy exponent is an artifact of the proof. An exact positive asymptotic constant rules out any uniform exponent improvement over the stated class, and the witness remains genuinely dissipative for every \(\gamma>0\). The exact one-site marginal simultaneously shows that this model has a faster local trace rate than the generic Pinsker consequence, clarifying what the global entropy sharpness does and does not control. This is a motivated structural boundary result rather than a routine parameter substitution.
